text: Empty files with unrecognised extensions (e.g. .gitkeep) are logged as error: unparseable in KB records and skipped from symbol extraction
File Documenter skips files with KB error:unparseable and logs a warning to .aee/document-warnings.md rather than fabricating content
On first run (no prior .aee/changed-files.json), the Repo Checker treats all files under src/ as added using git ls-files rather than git diff
Security Analyzer skips files with KB error:unparseable (e.g. empty or unrecognised-extension files) and logs a warning to .aee/security-warnings.md
File Intake Classifier flags files with unrecognised or absent extensions as language UNKNOWN in intake.jsonl and intake-summary.md rather than guessing; these are surfaced for human review

When only a subset of the expected 6 components has been delivered, the Relationship Linker records all potential seam partners as open ends and states which join-key categories produced nothing, rather than reporting zero findings as final

When only a subset of expected components has been delivered, the Synthesizer writes a 'delivery is partial' note in the Cross-Component Interfaces section rather than leaving it empty or omitting the section

The Synthesizer writes a stub doc (src.md in this run) for any component whose sole files are KB error:unparseable, noting the UNKNOWN file and flagging it for human triage — no separate UNKNOWN.md is created when the component field itself is not UNKNOWN

Cross-File Security Correlator upgrades severity by one level only when a confirmed taint chain crosses at least one crossComponent:true hop in the Link Graph; intra-component chains retain the original severity from the Security findings
Dependency Analyzer scans the full repository tree (not just /src) for pom.xml, requirements.txt, package.json, and go.mod; writes empty artifacts and exits cleanly when none are found

Infrastructure Analyzer writes infrastructure-secrets.json locally and registers it as an artifact but never stages or commits it to git; the file holds detected secret patterns and is explicitly excluded from commits
Infrastructure Analyzer writes empty artifacts and exits cleanly when no Dockerfiles, Terraform files, or Kubernetes YAML manifests are found anywhere in the repository

License Compliance Analyzer writes empty component/conflict/gap arrays and null productLicense when no LICENSE*, NOTICE*, vendor/, or third_party/ files exist, then commits and exits cleanly without error

Verifier Critic stores revision-rounds.txt in .aee/ at the repo root (not in any meridian-sample-code/ subdirectory); treat AGENT-PROMPT.md path references as relative to the repo root when no such subdirectory exists

When no open issue or PR exists in the repository, the Verifier Critic skips the outcome-label step rather than creating a new issue/PR — the label step only applies when a live issue/PR is the pipeline trigger

Architecture Artifact Generator always checks the readiness gate (all 5 required artifacts present) after syncing agent_workspace before writing any output files; if any artifact is missing it replies [PASS] and stops immediately

File Intake Classifier classifies .env.example (dotenv template) and requirements.txt (pip manifest) as language UNKNOWN since neither extension appears in the recognised source-extension list (.c/.h/.cpp/.java/.py/.go/.js/.mjs/.cjs/.ts); both are flagged for human review

aurora-portal pipeline-stage modules (adapter, collector, dispatcher, formatter, indexer, notifier, publisher, resolver, throttle, validator) all share identical class structure: __init__/handle/transform/stats methods plus a module-level build() factory; no external dependencies
File Documenter checks .agent-studio/artifacts.jsonl for existing Doc: entries before processing to avoid re-documenting files that were covered in a prior run
Security Analyzer marks findings as needs_cross_file when the dangerous sink is visible in the file but the taint source (function parameter origin or caller) is in a different file not yet seen
Dependency Analyzer re-runs a full manifest scan every invocation regardless of prior empty results; new manifests added by other agents between runs will be picked up on the next fast-forward pull

License Compliance Analyzer notes LGPL-2.1 (paramiko) as a weak-copyleft advisory in license-summary.md when the dependency appears in requirements.txt but is not vendored — dynamic pip installation does not trigger LGPL obligations, but vendoring would
Infrastructure Analyzer re-scans the full repository on every invocation and updates the summary if the source inventory has changed, even when the infrastructure file count remains zero

Relationship Linker records 5 open-end seams for aurora-portal: bus topic aurora.telemetry.tenant (consumer side), executable aurora-cli (caller side), subcommands profile-apply and profile-list (caller side), database table tenant_region_assignment (reader side) — all await partner components to become full cross-component seams

seam_index.py component_of() uses the first path segment relative to src/ as the component name; 'payload_plaintext' is the component for all aurora-portal files because the repo places them under src/payload_plaintext/
The Synthesizer registers each new Component:<name> artifact individually with aee-artifact add, then commits docs/components/ and .agent-studio/artifacts.jsonl together in one commit before pushing

When the Link Graph unresolved array lists open-end seams (bus.subscribe, cursor.execute, etc.), the Synthesizer describes them in the Cross-Component Interfaces section as open ends, not as confirmed seams, and notes the partner component has not yet arrived

Verifier Critic applies 'wrong-citation' (severity: error) when a component doc describes the content of a cited source line inaccurately — e.g. wrong command string — even when the line number itself is correct

Cross-File Security Correlator confirms chain-002 from telemetry_consumer.py: bus.subscribe() being unresolved in the Link Graph does not prevent chain confirmation when the consume()->handle()->yaml.load() data flow is fully traceable within the delivered source — only the producer side is unknown

When no callers of a vulnerable function (export_report, region_for, load_quota_profile) exist in the delivered source tree, the Cross-File Security Correlator records a partial chain with stoppedAt=function-entry and a gap note directing humans to find call sites in missing components (Django views, URL routing)

Architecture Artifact Generator re-runs all four docs/architecture/ documents on every invocation after the readiness gate passes, overwriting the prior run — the commit captures the delta; downstream agents should read the artifacts, not the prior commit

File Intake Classifier classifies go.mod (Go module manifest) as language UNKNOWN since extension .mod is not in the recognised source-extension list — consistent with how requirements.txt is handled; flagged for human review

aurora-compute service packages (audit, billing, dnsproxy, imaging, keystore, loadbalancer, metering, migration, placement, scheduler2, snapshot, telemetry) all share identical Record/Store pattern: Record struct, ErrNotFound var, Store with map, NewStore/Put/Get/ByProject/Total/Normalise/Count — no external deps, no side effects

Security Analyzer treats exec.Command("sh","-c",...) with fmt.Sprintf interpolation as a confirmed Go command-injection sink (CWE-78) even when the caller is unknown — confidence is needs_cross_file, not informational

Security Analyzer flags cgo boundaries where HTTP request body fields are passed as C strings without length or content validation as manual CWE-20 findings (needs_cross_file) when the C function definition is in a cross-component header not present in the repository

aurora-compute uniform service files (audit, billing, dnsproxy, imaging, keystore, loadbalancer, metering, migration, placement, scheduler2, snapshot, telemetry/telemetry) all follow the identical Record/Store pattern with no security sinks — confirmed clean on 2026-10-06 analysis

File Intake Classifier may require retries for the final git push if the platform credential (GitHub PAT / SSH key) for the agent owner is not yet registered; local commits are safe and no rework is needed — re-running the push step succeeds once credentials are added

Security Analyzer must run aee-toolchain doctor at the start of every invocation and record any MISSING scanner in .aee/security-warnings.md before proceeding — absence of toolchain does not block manual analysis but must be disclosed

Gitleaks does not flag AKIAIOSFODNN7EXAMPLE (AWS documentation example key — on its allowlist) nor plain-password strings like DATABASE_PASSWORD that lack a standard token format; hardcoded credential findings of this type require manual inspection
Bandit -ll filters findings below MEDIUM severity; B311 (random PRNG for cryptographic use) is LOW severity and will not appear in a -ll run — any random-for-secrets finding must be produced manually
Semgrep p/security-audit and p/owasp-top-ten rulesets do not flag exec.Command(sh,-c,...) Go shell injection; that pattern requires manual analysis

Fact Extractor should run aee-inventory --pretty and lizard --csv at the start of each batch (output to /tmp/scan/) and use tool output as source of truth for symbol names, kinds, line ranges, NLOC and CCN — manual extraction is only a fallback for symbols the tools miss
